plan_content.architectural_approach: Independence lens: I read from the consumer and contract end backward — enforcement step, then observe payload outputs, then the header's stated invariant, then the job gate — and met the changed code last, so the plan is anchored on the file's own declared contract rather than on implementation shape. The architectural move is to make the code honor the invariant it already states: dispatch the healthcheck outcome through an explicit exit-class case (docker-refusal 125/126/127 versus the probe's own exit status) so the branch that prints rpo=breached is unreachable when the probe could not run, mirroring the case dispatch the dr_observed branch already uses. Fail-closed is preserved, not weakened: indeterminate still fails the run, but with a message that names the cannot-tell class instead of asserting a breach. One bounded retry on the cannot-tell class only (single re-exec within the existing 120-second SSH command budget) hardens against the mid-restart transient the header itself names, without ever retrying a verdict. Boundary honesty: the healthcheck script's internal exit semantics are external to this file and are honored as verdicts when the script actually ran; what becomes structurally impossible is emitting a breach verdict the probe never produced.
plan_content.context: What this workflow is and why the failure matters, in cause/effect terms. A junior engineer should read it this way: (1) every five minutes, GitHub schedules this workflow on main; its only product is a green or red check plus step logs — if it fails persistently, operators either page on it or learn to ignore it, and an ignored RPO monitor is functionally absent. (2) The probe step SSHes to the production droplet and runs a payload that reports what production PROVES: dr_observed=present|absent|indeterminate, and, when archiving is present, rpo=healthy|breached. (3) The file's header states the governing invariant: only the first two observations are verdicts; 'could not tell' fails closed in resolve-dr-activation.sh rather than guessing — this discipline exists because the previous single docker exec collapsed everything into an opaque exit 127 (the INFRA-CRITICAL-195 history referenced in recent commits). (4) The rpo branch breaks that invariant: 'if docker exec ... postgres-walg-healthcheck.sh; then healthy else breached' treats docker-level refusal (daemon error 125, not-executable 126, not-found 127 — the probe never ran) identically to the healthcheck running and reporting the RPO budget unmet. Effect: a container mid-restart or an image whose script path moved produces a standing 'PRODUCTION WAL ARCHIVE RPO BREACH' alarm on main every five minutes, indistinguishable in the check status from a real breach. (5) If skipped, the next real breach is masked by noise and the invariant spec that runs this payload keeps locking the conflation in. Evidence proving the result after the fix: the failing run's step name plus the new class-labeled error message name exactly which of the three states fired, and the declared test command keeps the spec that executes this payload green.

key_changes.description: Diagnose the root cause of the failing 'Database WAL Archive Freshness' run on head 08b0f4d19fce2484ad528d45b0ebd903e7c1e71f and land the architectural fix, touching only .github/workflows/database-wal-archive-freshness.yml. Step A (diagnosis): read the failing run's log and record which of the five failure exits fired — 'Require protected main authority' (ref mismatch), 'Assert protected backup environment is complete' (missing DROPLET_* secrets), 'Observe production WAL archive runtime' (SSH transport or unrecognizable observation), 'Resolve declared activation against production' (declared/observed drift in either direction, or indeterminate failing closed), or 'Enforce the five-minute RPO' (rpo != healthy while active). Step B (fix, same file): in the observe payload's rpo branch, capture the docker exec exit status and classify it — exit 125/126/127 means the probe could not run: retry once after a short sleep within the existing 120-second command budget, and if it still cannot run print 'rpo=indeterminate'; a probe that ran and returned non-zero prints 'rpo=breached'; zero prints 'rpo=healthy'. In the observe step's output guard, additionally validate that rpo is one of healthy|breached|indeterminate whenever observed=present, so an empty or garbled rpo cannot flow onward. In the 'Enforce the five-minute RPO' step, distinguish three outcomes: healthy passes with the existing success message; breached keeps the existing breach error; indeterminate fails closed with an error that names the cannot-tell class and the retry result instead of asserting a breach. Leave the DR_CAPABILITY/DR_OBSERVED interface to resolve-dr-activation.sh, the env-scrubbed run-protected-ssh.sh invocation, and the payload's stdout key=value contract unchanged.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. Diagnosis (no file edit): open the failing run at head 08b0f4d and identify the failed step. Each of the five steps is one root-cause class; record the class and the step's error line in the commit message. This is mechanical because each class has a distinct step name.

2. Observe payload rpo branch: replace the unconditional if/else around 'docker exec aqua-postgres /usr/local/bin/postgres-walg-healthcheck.sh' with exit-class dispatch: capture the exec status; 125/126/127 -> single bounded retry (short sleep, one re-exec, still inside SSH_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120), still cannot-run -> printf 'rpo=indeterminate'; ran and non-zero -> 'rpo=breached'; zero -> 'rpo=healthy'. Never retry a verdict.

3. Observe step output guard: extend the existing case validation so that when observed=present, rpo must match healthy|breached|indeterminate; anything else hits the existing 'no recognisable observation' error path.

4. Enforcement step: three labeled outcomes — healthy: existing success message; breached: existing 'PRODUCTION WAL ARCHIVE RPO BREACH' error; indeterminate: fail closed with an error naming the cannot-tell class and the retry result, citing that a verdict was not obtainable.

5. Interface freeze: DR_OBSERVED/DR_CAPABILITY inputs to resolve-dr-activation.sh, the assert-backup-secrets.sh invocation, the run-protected-ssh.sh env-scrubbed invocation, and the payload stdout key=value shape all remain byte-compatible except for the one new rpo value.
6. Commit with the diagnosed root-cause class named, then run both declared validation commands.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 2 (make the correct behaviour the zero-effort default), achieved per defect: (1) the CORS matcher makes loopback-only approval the default response of the dev server — no per-developer action, no per-line pragma, and any non-loopback origin is refused structurally by configuration; (2) the spread-first key order makes the documented project-level test contract win by construction — precedence is enforced by object-literal evaluation order itself, so the project setup file cannot be shadowed without an explicit, visible edit to these lines. Both fixes are declarative and local; neither adds imports (imports: []) nor touches any file outside web/modules/admin-panel/vite.config.ts.
plan_content.context: Task, taught plainly: F-014 cites two lines of the admin-panel microfrontend's Vite config, and the fix must land in that one file. Start from the consumers and work backward. Consumer 1 is the module-federation host: in dev it fetches http://localhost:3004/remotes/admin-panel/remoteEntry.js cross-origin, which is why the server block has CORS at all — but 'cors: true' (line 47) answers 'yes' to EVERY Origin header, so any web page you have open can read responses from your dev server, not just the shell. Consumer 2 is the test runner: the 'test' object feeds all 50 spec files of project web-admin-panel, and its last key is the spread of the shared policy factory '...createVitestTestPolicy()' (line 57). In JavaScript object literals a later spread wins, so the shared policy silently outranks 'environment', 'globals', and 'setupFiles' (lines 54-56) — yet the comment at lines 51-52 calls exactly those keys 'a project-level runtime contract'. If libs/testing ever defines 'setupFiles', this project's setup file stops loading with no error and no failing test: that is the failure this plan removes. If skipped, the over-open CORS posture persists and the next change to the shared policy can silently alter test runtime for this module. Downstream surfaces: the shell's dev-time fetch of remoteEntry.js, the nx 'test' target of web-admin-panel with its 50 spec files, and the read-only contracts this config consumes (libs/testing policy factory, web/shared-ui federation helpers, pagination/shared-contracts aliases) — none of which are written. Evidence: the cited lines themselves in the provided excerpt; the three overlapping excerpts agree byte-for-byte on their overlap, which is the fidelity check used here because no file tools were available in this run to recompute the excerpt hashes.

key_changes.description: Edit web/modules/admin-panel/vite.config.ts only. (1) Line 47: keep 'port: 3004' and 'strictPort: true' unchanged and replace 'cors: true' with a restricted origin policy: cors: { origin: /^https?:\/\/(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|\[::1\])(:\d+)?$/ } — the config declares no server.host, so Vite binds loopback by default and every origin that can legitimately reach this remote is a loopback origin on an arbitrary port (the shell dev server). (2) Lines 53-57: move the '...createVitestTestPolicy()' spread to the FIRST key of the 'test' object so the keys that follow — 'environment: jsdom', 'globals: true', 'setupFiles: ["./src/test-setup.ts"]' (line 56) — take precedence over any same-named key the shared policy defines; the three values and the policy spread itself stay byte-identical, only key order changes. Keep formatting compliant with the repository format gate.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. Confirm the working tree matches the excerpt: server block at line 47 reads 'server: { port: 3004, strictPort: true, cors: true }' and the test block at lines 53-57 lists environment/globals/setupFiles before the createVitestTestPolicy() spread. If the file drifted, stop and surface the mismatch instead of editing blind.

2. Line 47 edit: replace 'cors: true' with 'cors: { origin: /^https?:\/\/(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1|\[::1\])(:\d+)?$/ }', keeping 'port: 3004' and 'strictPort: true' exactly as they are. Rationale chain: no server.host in this config -> Vite binds loopback -> every origin able to reach the dev server is loopback -> reflecting arbitrary origins grants nothing legitimate and exposes dev responses to any page.

3. Test-block edit: move '...createVitestTestPolicy()' to be the first key inside 'test', followed by 'environment: "jsdom"', 'globals: true', 'setupFiles: ["./src/test-setup.ts"]'. Change nothing else in the object; the policy's non-colliding keys (include, coverage, mock settings, etc.) continue to apply unchanged.
4. Run the four declared validation commands and require exit 0 on each; 'npx nx affected --target=test' is the decisive gate because it executes the 50 spec files under the reordered test object.
5. If any validation fails, revert the file (see rollback) and report rather than iterating outside the allowed surface.
plan_content.recursive_impact: Closure is the single nx project web-admin-panel (layer 3), which the changed path itself reaches. Inside it: (a) the project's test target and its 50 spec files inherit the reordered test object — the reorder only changes which side wins on key collision, and is verified by 'npx nx affected --target=test'; (b) dev-time consumers of remoteEntry.js see a CORS response restricted to loopback origins — production serving is unaffected because it does not use this dev-server option; (c) build/preview outputs are untouched (no change to exposes, shared, base, build.target). No event-contract, NATS consumer, entity, or migration surface is touched, so the machine closure adds no nodes beyond project:web-admin-panel; no waivers are needed. The read-only contracts (libs/testing/vitest policy, web/shared-ui federation config and alias helper, platform/libs/pagination-contracts, libs/shared-contracts) are consumed, never written; notably the reorder fix is correct regardless of what keys the policy factory returns, so the plan does not depend on unread internals of libs/testing.

plan_content.summary: Independent consumer-first scan of web/modules/admin-panel/vite.config.ts finds exactly two remediable defects on the cited lines. plan_content.title: Fix failing CI workflow 'Deploy Capacity Maintenance' (run #38409794036)

plan_content.architectural_approach: Defect chain, stated as cause and effect: the script does 'cd /var/aqua-saas' — the file's own comment documents this is a bare object store, not a working tree — then 'git fetch --force --prune origin main'. A shorthand refspec fetch writes FETCH_HEAD only; a bare clone has no configured remote.origin.fetch refspec, so no opportunistic remote-tracking update creates or refreshes refs/remotes/origin/main. The next line, 'TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse origin/main)"', resolves the 'origin/main' shorthand against exactly those remote-tracking refs — which the store does not guarantee to exist. Under 'set -euo pipefail' that resolution failure exits the step before checkout bootstrap, failing every scheduled and dispatched run identically. Even if the store happens to carry local configuration that makes the shorthand resolve today, depending on undocumented store state is itself the defect. Fix, tier 2 (make the correct behaviour the zero-effort default): fetch with the fully-qualified refspec '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' and read 'refs/remotes/origin/main' — the write and the read name the identical fully-qualified ref in adjacent commands, so correct pinning requires no operator effort and no store-side setup, and the failure mode has no ambient state left to depend on.
plan_content.context: What this lane is and why the failure matters: 'Deploy Capacity Maintenance' is the production droplet's 6-hourly capacity lane. Each production deploy pulls a fresh image per service (~1.85GB x 13) and leaves the prior generation untagged; this workflow's safe-image-gc keeps the droplet under the capacity-preflight threshold so deploys do not block — the workflow's own header names run #695 / 28332208818 / 28330781676 as the historic blocked-deploy outcome. The job (line 54) has one SSH step (line 59) that must: derive and validate a GHCR image prefix from github.repository (INFRA-CRITICAL-085: no dispatch input names a release, image, registry or repository), resolve the remote's current main to a pinned SHA on the droplet's bare object store, bootstrap the immutable deploy checkout from that SHA, and run scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh from it. It is failing on head 99689e46bd86eb980ca2bad74df3c6b072eb4e90. The task: diagnose the root cause and land the architectural fix touching only this workflow file. If it is skipped or mis-fixed, untagged generations accumulate until production deploys are capacity-blocked — the exact outage class this lane exists to prevent; the downstream surface is the deploy control plane's capacity preflight and the droplet's disk headroom.

key_changes.description: Root-cause fix in the capacity-maintenance step's script block (the step whose name begins 'Run capacity operation through production deploy control plane'). Replace the two lines 'git fetch --force --prune origin main' and 'TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse origin/main)"' with 'git fetch --force --prune origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' and 'TARGET_SHA="$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main)"'. Effect: the fetch explicitly writes the fully-qualified remote-tracking ref and the pin reads that same fully-qualified ref, so SHA resolution cannot depend on the bare store's ambient refspec configuration; 'cd /var/aqua-saas', the DEPLOY_SHA export, and everything after (install -d /var/lib/aqua/deploy, git show of deploy-paths.sh, materialize_deploy_checkout, the OPERATION case block) stay byte-identical.

Adjacent hardening in the same script block, same file: immediately after 'export DEPLOY_SHA="${TARGET_SHA}"' add 'printf "capacity lane pinned to %s\n" "${DEPLOY_SHA}"' so the resolved pin is visible in the job log for triage, and add a short comment above the fetch stating the invariant — the store is bare and carries no remote-tracking configuration guarantee, so the lane must fetch and read the same fully-qualified ref — so a future editor cannot silently regress to shorthand resolution.

plan_content.summary: The capacity-maintenance job fails in its single SSH step when it pins the target SHA: the script fetches 'main' into the droplet's bare object store with a shorthand refspec (which writes FETCH_HEAD only, since bare stores carry no remote.origin.fetch refspec to update opportunistically) and then resolves the 'origin/main' shorthand, which depends on remote-tracking refs the store does not maintain; under 'set -euo pipefail' the step exits before checkout bootstrap and the 6-hourly GC lane fails on every scheduled and manual run. The fix, entirely inside the one allowed file, makes SHA resolution configuration-independent: fetch with the fully-qualified refspec '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' and read 'refs/remotes/origin/main', so the ref written and the ref read are the same name in adjacent commands. This is tier 2 — correct resolution becomes the zero-effort default with no reliance on undocumented store state. Residual risk: run logs are not admissible evidence here, so if the observed failure sits past bootstrap (inside scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh at the target commit, or at the SSH command_timeout) the fix locus is outside allowed_scope and the round must widen scope instead of landing this edit.

plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier 2 — make the correct behaviour automatic. Today the correct CI status for a completed maintenance sweep requires a human to look at a red check and mentally reclassify it as 'expected while degraded'; after the change, green-when-the-bounded-contract-completed is the zero-effort default, and degradation becomes a surfaced, greppable warning instead of a false maintenance failure. Blocking semantics are preserved where they belong: manual 'gate' dispatch propagates the raw verdict, and the deploy-time gate in the deploy workflows is independent of this lane. A Tier-3 detectability component rides along: stage markers plus RC capture make any future failure self-locating, which also closes the diagnosis loop that the evidence set (file only, no logs) could not. The capacity finding itself is never hidden — it is reclassified to a non-blocking, explicitly-marked channel while every hard-failure class (bootstrap errors, script kills, timeouts, unsupported operation) stays red.
plan_content.context: What this lane does, for orientation: every 6 hours (cron, line 15) GitHub Actions SSHes to the production droplet, resolves origin/main inside the bare store /var/aqua-saas, bootstraps the canonical immutable deploy checkout from that exact SHA, and runs scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh — 'report' or 'gate' for manual dispatch, 'gate' with CAPACITY_GC_MODE=auto for the scheduled sweep that reclaims superseded images (~1.85GB x 13 per deploy generation per the header). Why the failure shape matters: the CI run on head 99689e46 failed with annotations anchored at the job (line 54) and the single step (line 59), i.e. the SSH step exited non-zero — but the evidence set contains no run log, so the diagnosis must come from the file's structure. The structural cause: under 'set -euo pipefail' the script's last command is the capacity gate (line 110), and the header itself (lines 5-14) defines that gate as a deploy-blocking control that 'blocks' when disk accumulates. A maintenance lane whose success criterion is a deploy-blocking gate will report itself as failed precisely in the situation it exists to manage — whenever the bounded GC cannot fully clear the capacity class (non-image disk growth such as volumes, logs, or build cache under the pull-only ADR-033 runtime, or a residual class after the sweep stops at its bound). What breaks if this is skipped: a permanently or frequently red scheduled check that trains operators to ignore it, hiding genuine regressions in the bootstrap chain inside the noise. Downstream surfaces affected by the fix: the scheduled lane's own CI status (intended), any branch-protection rule that references this workflow by name (its meaning changes from 'capacity healthy' to 'maintenance executed' — documented in kc-3), and nothing on the droplet itself, since the same script, environment, and bounds are run unchanged.

key_changes.description: Instrument the SSH script in .github/workflows/deploy-capacity-maintenance.yml with greppable stage markers and explicit exit-code capture. Echo a line like '[capacity-maintenance] stage=image-prefix' around the IMAGE_PREFIX derivation/validation, 'stage=bare-store-fetch' around the /var/aqua-saas fetch and rev-parse, 'stage=checkout-bootstrap' around the deploy-paths.sh bootstrap and materialize_deploy_checkout, and 'stage=capacity-op' around the droplet-capacity.sh invocation. Replace the unconditional capacity invocation in the case branch with 'set +e; CAPACITY_GC_MODE=auto CAPACITY_DISK_USAGE_MODE=deep bash scripts/deploy/droplet-capacity.sh gate; RC=$?; set -e' so the gate's verdict is captured rather than terminating the script. This makes each future failure localize to its exact stage in the run log (the current evidence anchors only the job at line 54 and the step at line 59) and is the in-band instrument that confirms or refutes the structural diagnosis on the next run.

Split the shared 'safe-image-gc | gate' case branch (line 109) into two branches with distinct success contracts. safe-image-gc (the scheduled maintenance path, OPERATION fallback at line 65): if RC=0 exit 0 unchanged; if RC!=0 emit a distinct non-blocking marker — echo '::warning::capacity maintenance completed its bounded sweep; capacity class not cleared — full gate output above' and 'MAINTENANCE-OUTCOME=capacity-degraded' — then exit 0. gate (manual workflow_dispatch): propagate RC unchanged so a human-dispatched capacity check remains blocking. Everything before the case statement (bootstrap chain, lines 88-103) stays under 'set -e' and remains a hard failure, and kills at command_timeout 12m (line 76) or timeout-minutes 15 (line 56) never reach the classifier, so only returned gate verdicts are reclassified. Net effect: the lane's CI status asserts 'the bounded maintenance executed' automatically, while the deploy lane's own capacity preflight remains the blocking capacity control.

Update the header comment block (lines 5-14) and the OPERATION-fallback comment (lines 62-64) to state the lane's success contract explicitly: scheduled safe-image-gc equals bounded sweep executed (green); residual capacity class equals warning marker in the log with the blocking control living in the deploy-time gate; infrastructure/bootstrap errors and timeout kills equal red. Note in the comment that the remote '::warning::' and '::error::' strings are log markers, not GitHub annotations, because appleboy/ssh-action does not forward workflow commands emitted on the droplet — which is also true of the existing '::error::' uses in the script today.

plan_steps_detailed: 1. kc-1: add stage markers and convert the capacity invocation in the case branch to captured-RC form (set +e ... RC=$? ... set -e).
2. kc-2: split 'safe-image-gc | gate' into two branches; scheduled GC path exits 0 with a warning marker on RC!=0; manual gate path propagates RC.
3. kc-3: update header and OPERATION-fallback comments to document the success contract and the marker-not-annotation nature of remote workflow-command strings.

4. Verify: run the declared validation commands; after landing, inspect the next scheduled run's log for the stage markers and outcome marker, and confirm a manual operation=gate dispatch on a degraded droplet still exits non-zero.

plan_content.title: Give the Deploy Capacity Maintenance lane its own success contract instead of inheriting the deploy-blocking capacity gate's exit code
plan_content.validation_plan: Static gates from the operator-declared canonical suite: 'npx nx affected --target=lint', 'npm run type-check', 'node tools/quality/quality.mjs format check-changed' — all expected exit 0 (the change is YAML-only, so the code graph is unaffected and these prove no collateral breakage plus format compliance). Behavioral proof, post-land: the next scheduled run's log contains the stage markers and, on a degraded droplet, the MAINTENANCE-OUTCOME marker with a green conclusion; a manually dispatched operation=gate run against the same droplet state exits non-zero, proving blocking semantics survived the split; a run that fails during bootstrap (if ever) still fails red, proving the hard-failure classes were not weakened.

risks.recommendation: Treat the primary's own plan step 3 as a binding landing precondition: the implementer must confirm the failing run's error class is 'unknown revision' / 'ambiguous argument origin/main' at the fetch/rev-parse stage; a death past bootstrap stops the edit and triggers a re-plan with widened scope instead of landing.
risks.summary: The primary's diagnosis is unconfirmed by any run log in the admissible evidence set, and whether refs/remotes/origin/main exists on the droplet's bare store is unobservable within allowed_scope; if the store already carries the remote-tracking ref (for example seeded by the deploy control plane's own fetches), the shorthand pair resolves today and the prescribed edit is a robustness improvement that does not remediate the observed failure, whose real locus would then be the gate-verdict class the challenger names. The primary discloses this (R1, plan step 3) but the entire fix's efficacy rides on it.

risks.recommendation: Converge on the union that de-risks both hypotheses: the primary's key_changes[0] refspec pair plus the challenger's kc-1 stage markers, with the gate exit semantics unchanged; admit kc-2/kc-3 only after a post-landing run log shows the gate-verdict class is the live failure.
risks.summary: Neither plan alone covers both live-failure hypotheses: the primary fixes the pinning pair but adds only a single success log line (kc-hardening-observability-001), while the challenger owns the stage-marker instrument (kc-1) that would adjudicate the divergence on the very next run, yet packages it with the exit-code reclassification instead of with the pinning fix; the observability pieces overlap (the primary's log line is a subset of the challenger's markers).

risks.recommendation: Gate any success-contract change on evidence that the failing run reached the capacity gate at all: adopt the primary's fully-qualified refspec pair ('+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main' with 'git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/main') as a prerequisite key change, or require implementer-side run-log confirmation of the failing stage before kc-2 lands.
risks.summary: The two plans fix different hypothesized defects and only one can be the live root cause of failing run ci-run-38409794036: the challenger's diagnosis never considers the file-documented bare-store shorthand-resolution failure (a fetch with the bare refspec 'main' writes FETCH_HEAD only, and 'git rev-parse origin/main' then depends on refs/remotes/origin/main existing on a store the file's own comment documents as bare), so if that mode is live, kc-1/kc-2/kc-3 leave the scheduled lane failing exactly as before while the CI-semantics change lands without delivering its claimed benefit. The challenger's step-level annotation anchors (:54/:59) cannot localize the failure inside the script, and its own R-2 lists bootstrap-stage errors but omits this specific rev-parse resolution failure.

risks.recommendation: Keep the scheduled verdict blocking until droplet-capacity.sh exposes a distinguishable exit-code contract (a separately scoped change with its own evidence), or reclassify only one narrowly defined RC value while every other non-zero RC stays red.
risks.summary: kc-2 cannot distinguish a genuine capacity-verdict exit code from an internal error of droplet-capacity.sh (that script is beyond this round's allowed_scope), so once the scheduled path exits 0 on any non-zero RC, a future regression inside the gate script reports green on the 6-hourly lane; the challenger discloses this as R-1 at MEDIUM severity, which under-weights a scheduled monitoring channel that can go silently wrong exactly when operators rely on it.
